title: Control finite-horizon arbitrary predictable faults using nominal all-mark entropy
statement: Compare complete fine ALL-marked path laws P0/Pa on [0,T], retaining the external policy seed and causal rule on a common filtered space. The policy may use the entire past, including hidden/null/parallel marks. Localized exact log(dP0/dPa)=-sum_marks log a_e+integral sum_e(a_e-1)lambda_e0. Nominal expectation gives D(P0||Pa)=E0 integral sum lambda_e0[-log a_e+a_e-1]<=2delta^2 E0 F_all(T), delta<=1/2. Localize population, count and integrated intensity first; nominal finite work, increasing-filtration entropy and nonexplosion yield the full-record bound. Pinsker with supremum-event TV gives TV<=delta sqrt(E0 F_all(T)). Decoding, erasing hidden labels and time rescaling cannot increase TV; external randomness is marginalized after comparison. Rational J>=nominal expected work and an integer square-root ceiling allow delta<=epsilon/[4max(1,ceil(sqrt J))], without observing physical counts. These are standard likelihood/Girsanov/Pinsker principles, not a priority claim. Finite-horizon accuracy does not bound unbounded faulty supremum or all-firing expectations or all-time moments; rare large costs remain unpaid and the full reversible adaptive compiler remains open.
